Objective
Factor the greatest common factor, or GCF, from every term in a polynomial.
Factoring reverses distribution
Twelve x plus eighteen equals six times the quantity two x plus three. Expanding checks the answer.
Numerical factor
The greatest common divisor of eighteen and twenty four is six. Choose the largest shared coefficient.
Variables
For x cubed and x squared, keep x squared. Use the smaller shared exponent.
Two variables
Eighteen x cubed y squared plus twenty four x squared y cubed equals six x squared y squared times three x plus four y.
Three terms
Twenty a cubed b minus thirty a squared b squared plus ten a b equals ten a b times two a squared minus three a b plus one.
Missing variables
Fourteen m squared n plus twenty one m n squared plus thirty five m has GCF seven m. The last term has no n.
Negative coefficients
Negative fifteen a squared b plus twenty five a b squared equals five a b times negative three a plus five b.
Check by expanding
Distribute the common factor back into every term. The original coefficients, variables, exponents and signs must return.
Geometry application
Area eighteen x squared plus thirty x, divided by width six x, gives rectangle length three x plus five.
Unknown exponents
If the GCF contains x cubed, the smaller exponent among the original terms must be three.
Exam recap
Find the coefficient GCF, use variables common to every term with minimum exponents, divide, then expand to check.
